lines.say: Louisiana, around 2000. A two-year-old boy named James Leininger starts having nightmares. Screaming: airplane crash, on fire, can't get out.
shots: q: Louisiana bayou night || alt: swamp bayou night
q: vintage toy airplane on floor

lines.say: He talks about flying a Corsair, a World War Two fighter, from a ship called the Natoma.
shots: archive: F4U Corsair WWII photo (US Navy, public domain)
archive: USS Natoma Bay escort carrier (public domain)

lines.say: He says he had a friend there named Jack Larsen. And he says the pilot was named James, like him.
His father, a skeptic, starts researching to prove him wrong.
He finds the USS Natoma Bay. A pilot named Jack Larsen served on it. And one pilot from it was killed near Iwo Jima in 1945: James Huston Junior.
shots: archive: Natoma Bay squadron photo (public domain)
line art: name James M. Huston Jr. typed

lines.say: Skeptics point out the family visited an aviation museum before the nightmares, and that details sharpened as the parents researched.
shots: line art: timeline showing museum visit

lines.say: Researchers at the University of Virginia call it one of their strongest American cases. Both readings are still on the table.
shots: q: University of Virginia rotunda || alt: old American university rotunda

fact_note: James Leininger case, Lafayette, Louisiana (KNOWN as reported: Leininger 'Soul Survivor' 2009; Tucker 'Return to Life' 2013). Corsair, Natoma Bay, Jack Larsen, James M. Huston Jr. killed 3 Mar 1945 near Iwo Jima/Chichi Jima (KNOWN). Huston was flying an FM-2 Wildcat when killed (note: James said Corsair; Huston had flown Corsairs earlier) (DEBATED detail). Critiques (KNOWN). Tie-in to 'Have You Lived Before?' Mon 26 Oct.
ig_caption: the dad was trying to disprove it. this is the case that made a lot of skeptics at least pause
tt_caption: James Leininger, the boy who remembered being a WWII pilot #reincarnation #pastlife

lines.say: Ian Stevenson was a psychiatrist at the University of Virginia. For forty years he collected cases of children who said they remembered a past life.
shots: q: University of Virginia campus autumn || alt: old American university campus autumn

lines.say: Some of those children had something physical. Birthmarks, or birth defects, in unusual places.
shots: line art: body outline with marks

lines.say: And the child would say: that's where I was shot. Or stabbed. In the life before.
shots: line art: speech bubble 'that's where I was shot'

lines.say: In 1993 he published a paper on two hundred and ten of these cases.
Where he could find autopsy reports or medical records for the person the child named, he said the wounds matched the marks in most of them.
shots: line art: two outlines, marks aligned

lines.say: Critics answer that the families often knew each other first, and that matching a story to a mark after the fact is easy.
shots: line art: arrows connecting two villages
q: village road Sri Lanka || alt: village road tropical

lines.say: It's still the most physical evidence anyone has offered for reincarnation, and it's still argued about.
shots: q: dusk over Blue Ridge mountains || alt: dusk over forested mountains

fact_note: Stevenson, 'Birthmarks and Birth Defects Corresponding to Wounds on Deceased Persons', J. Scientific Exploration 1993: 210 cases; in 43 of 49 cases with medical documents, correspondence confirmed (KNOWN as reported; say 'most'). Critiques: prior family contact, retrofitting (Edwards, Angel) (DEBATED). Tie-in to Mon 26 ep.
ig_caption: this is the part of the reincarnation research that surprised me most. physical marks, not just stories
tt_caption: Ian Stevenson's birthmark cases, the strangest reincarnation evidence #reincarnation #ianstevenson

hook: Pythagoras heard his dead friend|in a *puppy*

lines.say: Pythagoras is the triangle guy. He was also one of the first people in Greece to teach that souls are reborn.
shots: line art: right triangle fading to circle

lines.say: And the oldest story about him isn't about math. It's about a dog.
A poet named Xenophanes, who lived at the same time, wrote it down.
Pythagoras walks past a man beating a puppy. He stops him and says:
shots: line art: two outlines and a small dog

lines.say: Stop, don't hit it. It's the soul of a friend of mine. I recognized his voice when I heard it cry.
Xenophanes probably meant it as a joke. But it tells us that Pythagoras really did teach rebirth, even into animals. That's why his followers reportedly avoided eating meat.
shots: q: vegetables on wooden table rustic
line art: circle soul -> animal -> human

lines.say: Two and a half thousand years ago, the father of Western math believed you might come back with four legs.

fact_note: Xenophanes fr. 7 (Diogenes Laertius 8.36) (KNOWN). Satirical intent (KNOWN interpretation). Pythagorean metempsychosis (KNOWN). Pythagorean dietary restrictions (KNOWN in tradition; extent DEBATED).
ig_caption: the oldest story we have about Pythagoras is him telling a guy to stop hitting a puppy because it's his reincarnated friend

hook: The past life that came from|*across the street*

lines.say: In 1952, in Colorado, a businessman hypnotized a housewife named Virginia Tighe.
shots: q: 1950s Colorado town archive || alt: 1950s American mountain town archive

lines.say: Under hypnosis, she started speaking in an Irish accent. She said she was Bridey Murphy, born in Cork in 1798.
shots: q: Cork Ireland old street || alt: old European old street

lines.say: The tapes became a bestselling book, The Search for Bridey Murphy. America went crazy for past lives.
Then newspapers went digging. No birth record of a Bridey Murphy in Cork was ever found.
shots: line art: search with no result

lines.say: And one paper reported that across the street from where Virginia grew up in Chicago lived an Irish immigrant named Bridie Murphy Corkell.
shots: q: Chicago 1930s street archive || alt: American city 1930s street archive
line art: two houses facing each other

lines.say: Psychologists have a word for this: cryptomnesia. Memories you've forgotten coming back, feeling like they were never yours.
That's why most researchers distrust hypnosis for past lives. It doesn't just recover memories. It can build them.

fact_note: Morey Bernstein hypnotized Virginia Tighe, Pueblo CO, 1952 (KNOWN). Book 1956 (KNOWN). Chicago American reports on Bridie Murphy Corkell (KNOWN; neighbor claim DEBATED, contested by supporters). Cryptomnesia (KNOWN term). Hypnosis can create false memories (KNOWN, Loftus et al.).
ig_caption: 1950s America lost its mind over this tape. then the newspapers found the neighbor
tt_caption: Bridey Murphy, the famous past life regression that unraveled #pastliferegression #hypnosis

lines.say: In the mountains of Lebanon, Syria and Israel live the Druze, a religious community of about a million people.
shots: q: Mount Lebanon villages aerial || alt: Mediterranean mountain villages aerial
q: Golan heights landscape || alt: dry highland heights landscape

lines.say: Their belief about death is unusual even among religions that accept reincarnation.
There's no waiting. No heaven in between. The moment a person dies, their soul enters a baby being born.
shots: line art: two clocks, same second
q: dawn breaking over hills time-lapse

lines.say: Always a human. Never an animal.
So when a small child starts talking about another family, another name, another village, Druze families don't panic. They have a word for it, nutq: the speech.
Sometimes the families visit each other. And the child gets two families instead of one.
Researchers have recorded some of the most detailed child cases among them.
shots: q: Lebanese mountains sunset || alt: Mediterranean mountains sunset

fact_note: Druze belief in immediate transmigration (taqamus) into a human (KNOWN). Population ~1 million (KNOWN approx). 'Nutq' for children's past-life speech (KNOWN). Stevenson and others studied Druze cases (KNOWN). Avoid naming specific children (privacy).
ig_caption: for the Druze there's no gap at all. you die and you're born in the same moment
tt_caption: the Druze belief in instant reincarnation #reincarnation #druze

lines.say: Buddhism teaches rebirth. It also teaches there's no permanent soul. So what exactly gets reborn?
shots: line art: question mark between two circles

lines.say: Around two thousand years ago, a Greek king in India asked a monk that exact question.
The king was Menander. The monk was Nagasena. Their conversation was written down as The Questions of King Milinda.
The king asks: is the one who is reborn the same person, or someone else? Nagasena says: neither the same, nor another.
Then he gives an example. Light a lamp in the evening. Is the flame at midnight the same flame? At dawn?
Not quite the same, not a different one either. One flame passed along, unbroken.
shots: line art: flame passing along a line

lines.say: In Buddhism, that's you. Not a thing that travels. A process that continues.

fact_note: Milindapanha, dialogue of Menander I (Indo-Greek king, 2nd c. BC) and Nagasena (KNOWN). 'Neither the same nor another' and lamp-through-the-night simile (KNOWN). Text compiled over time (KNOWN).
ig_caption: a Greek king asked a Buddhist monk how rebirth works without a soul. the candle answer is the best thing I've read this week
tt_caption: how Buddhist rebirth works without a soul, explained with a flame #buddhism #rebirth

lines.say: When the 13th Dalai Lama died in 1933, Tibet had to find his next incarnation. A child.
shots: q: Potala Palace Lhasa || alt: Himalayan palace

lines.say: The regent went to a sacred lake and reported seeing a vision on the water: three Tibetan letters, a monastery, and a house with turquoise roof tiles.
shots: q: Tibetan sacred lake high altitude
line art: three Tibetan letters Ah Ka Ma

lines.say: Search parties went out. One reached a village in the northeast, Taktser, and found a house that matched.
shots: q: Tibetan village mountains Amdo || alt: Tibetan village mountains high plateau

lines.say: The lama leading the search disguised himself as a servant. A two-year-old boy came straight to him and asked for the rosary he wore. It had belonged to the 13th Dalai Lama.
Later, the boy was shown pairs of objects: walking sticks, drums, rosaries. Each time, according to the searchers, he picked the one that had been his predecessor's.
shots: line art: two objects, one chosen

lines.say: That boy, Lhamo Thondup, became Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama.
shots: archive: 14th Dalai Lama as a child (public domain)

lines.say: Believers see recognition. Skeptics see a search that knew what it wanted to find.

fact_note: 13th Dalai Lama d. 1933 (KNOWN). Regent Reting's vision at Lhamo La-tso, letters Ah Ka Ma, house with turquoise tiles (KNOWN traditional account, Dalai Lama's autobiography). Kewtsang Rinpoche disguised as servant, rosary, object tests (KNOWN as account). Born 1935 Taktser (KNOWN). Check licence of child photo (1930s-40s photos; use only confirmed PD).
ig_caption: the rosary moment gives me chills every time, whatever you think about it
tt_caption: how the 14th Dalai Lama was found as a child #dalailama #tibet

hook: 3 patterns in kids who|*remember past lives*

lines.say: The University of Virginia has studied over two thousand five hundred children who say they remember a previous life. A few patterns keep showing up.
shots: q: University of Virginia lawn || alt: old American university lawn

lines.say: One. Timing. They usually start talking about it between two and three years old, and they mostly stop by six or seven.
Two. The past life often ended suddenly. A large share of these children describe a violent or unnatural death: accidents, drowning, war.
Three. The gap is short. In the cases where a previous person was identified, the time between that death and the child's birth is usually a year or two, not centuries.
shots: line art: two dates close together

lines.say: Some kids also show matching fears or habits, like fear of water when the previous person drowned.
Skeptics say these patterns come from how cases get reported and filtered. Researchers say that alone doesn't explain the details.

fact_note: UVA Division of Perceptual Studies: 2,500+ cases (KNOWN). Onset ~2-3, fade by ~6-7 (KNOWN, Tucker). ~70% report violent/unnatural death (Tucker) (KNOWN as reported; 'large share'). Median interval ~16 months (Tucker) (KNOWN as reported; 'a year or two'). Phobias related to mode of death (KNOWN as reported). Sampling-bias critique (DEBATED).
ig_caption: the 'they stop talking about it around 6 or 7' part is what makes parents go quiet
tt_caption: what children who remember past lives have in common #reincarnation #pastlives

hook: If we're reborn, where do|*new souls* come from?

lines.say: Here's the question that always comes up. In 1800 there were about one billion people. Now there are over eight billion. If everyone is reborn, where did the extra souls come from?
shots: line art: population graph 1 billion -> 8 billion

lines.say: Different traditions answer it differently.
Hindu and Buddhist thought say rebirth isn't only human. Animals, insects, other realms. Humans are a tiny fraction of all living beings, so the pool is huge.
Some modern believers say new souls are created all the time, and some people are on their first life.
Others suggest souls aren't countable at all, more like waves in one ocean than separate coins.
shots: line art: waves rising from one line

lines.say: None of these can be tested. But the math problem only works if you assume souls are like individual items. Most traditions never did.

fact_note: World population ~1 billion c. 1800, >8 billion 2022 (KNOWN). Hindu/Buddhist rebirth across species and realms (KNOWN). Other answers are SPECULATION; presented as positions, no endorsement.
ig_caption: my friend hit me with this question at dinner and I went down a rabbit hole. turns out most traditions saw it coming

lines.say: There's a popular claim: early Christians believed in reincarnation, until a church council deleted it in 553.
shots: q: Hagia Sophia interior || alt: Byzantine church interior

lines.say: Here's what actually happened. In 553, the Second Council of Constantinople did condemn ideas linked to an early theologian named Origen.
shots: q: Istanbul skyline Bosphorus || alt: old city skyline strait

lines.say: Origen taught that souls existed before birth. That part is real, and it was condemned.
shots: line art: soul before birth, crossed

lines.say: But Origen himself rejected reincarnation. He wrote against souls moving into new bodies.
shots: line art: arrow body -> body crossed

lines.say: And no Bible passages were removed at that council. The New Testament was settled long before.
The verse people point to is Jesus saying John the Baptist was Elijah. Christians have long read that as a role, not a rebirth. Others disagree.
shots: archive: John the Baptist painting (public domain)

lines.say: So: pre-existence of souls, condemned. Reincarnation deleted from the Bible: no evidence.
shots: line art: two stamps DEBATED / NO EVIDENCE
q: dust in church light beam

fact_note: Second Council of Constantinople 553 and anathemas against Origenism incl. pre-existence (KNOWN; whether anathemas were formally conciliar is DEBATED). Origen rejected metensomatosis (Contra Celsum, Commentary on Matthew) (KNOWN). NT canon broadly settled by late 4th c. (KNOWN). Matthew 11:14 / 17:12 Elijah readings (KNOWN, interpretation DEBATED).
ig_caption: I believed this one for years. the real story is weirder and way more specific
tt_caption: was reincarnation removed from the Bible in 553? #christianity #reincarnation
